st: How newspapers and authors remember the huge hole COVID left behind

sec.t: ff.27.1 The New York Times' pixels
sec.p: Over the last few years, The New York Times has been very attentive to the pandemic. I was struck by its report on Bergamo and the deaths of the first wave, with images taken directly from L'Eco di Bergamo and its countless pages “of the dead”.
Axios created another beautiful visualisation to put the victims and numbers of the pandemic in context: as you scroll this page, the dead pile up, as shown in the chart in the corner.

sec.t: ff.27.3 The Washington Post's unfinished sentences
sec.p: The Washington Post, on the other hand, presented a project with a series of unfinished sentences. It doesn't aim to show every detail of the problem, but asks us to stop and read a few stories. It's frustrating. Because the opening page looks like this:
